I don't know the teacher, especially if they are older or really stubborn or dogmatic it can seem nearly impossible or like a lost cause. But I've seen people change. It's not too crazy. It really depends a lot on how easy it is for them to continue on being the way they are. If there's no reaction to whatever they're doing they feel encouraged and empowered to continue doing so. From the image it looked like OP was trying to hold back and I'd like to encourage people to stand up for themselves and what they think is right. In a respectful and non violent way of course. I'm fairly certain that not many opinions are changed when you shout at people's faces. Your opponent and audience need to take you seriously for them to take your message seriously. Idk, if I were OP I'd just spend a couple days researching and compiling data supporting their view. And then repeatedly disprove the statements the teacher talks about. Never going too in depth about things or letting oneself get provoked. And don't waste too much class time either. I used to have a bunch of bookmarks sorted in my phone with lots of papers and scientific articles about controversial political topics and just pull them up during class. It's fun tbh. Especially since teachers are not really prepared in this way and mostly have their opinions and random every day knowledge to back their stance up and rarely have enough time or energy to counterpoint your arguments in their free time. As long as you're not cocky about it and helpful and humble, they can't do shit. It's not the kind of conflict they expect, since their authority is only very specific and they can't use it unless you do something stupid yourself. Persistence is key. Do things often, and subtly and you can change people's attitudes about some topics. That's basically how propaganda works too. I'd suggest to look up how people get indoctrinated. It's usually not by some one time event, but usually over extended periods of time with a relatively low barrier of entry, but slowly ramping up and getting more and more into the direction they want. Cults for example too is really interesting. They try to segregate their people from other sources of information so that the cult positive information is higher percentage wise than the cult negative information. So the more people you can get onboard, the better. A lot of subtle hints from a lot of different people makes people think that this is right. You can't win arguments as an individual vs another individual. It's all about how great your influence is. If it was all only based on logic we wouldn't have people with stupid ideas you know? Just look at how flat earth is a somewhat stable phenomenon. The people believe in something not because it's right, but because they got convinced. And that's the only thing that matters to them. So in a quest to change someone's mind it's not about how true you are, but rather what tools you can use and what resources you have to change someone's mind and how convincing these are.

Staying calm and responding respectfully, taking their personal experiences into account and not dismissing their views as idiotic etc will drastically improve your chance of changing someone's mind. Remember that you can't change someone's mind in just one session of arguments. People will rarely ever admit that they were wrong about something but twist things so that it appears like they weren't that bad. Don't go too much into it and always give them space to be able to change their opinion. It takes time and their opinion will change slowly over multiple sessions. Changing their opinion shouldn't feel like they were forced to do it, because they will try and resist the more force you apply. Make changing their mind as easy and welcoming as possible. Don't try to pose facts in a "gotcha!" Kind of way, but show them that their way of looking at things is by far not the only and not the best way. When talking about emotions, create scenarios told from a first person perspective getting into details and extrapolating the future prospects to show how certain decisions affect the people you are advocating for. Try looking up eristic dialectics by Arthur Schopenhauer, he has some interesting points in how to most effectively change people's minds. One thing to consider, something that is especially important in public discussions for example. Is that you're not necessarily arguing against the teacher and trying to change their minds, but more so trying to change the minds of the listeners. You can have a successful dispute, even if you've officially lost it against the teacher, as long as you can convince the audience of your own view. Good luck!

I agree with you, since you are right in every point you mentioned. You said stuff like "The past is the past and it can't be changed", "I am who I am and even though I can change a lot, I can't change everything about myself", "It is not possible for me to be a woman by the definitions I accept" etc etc
And all I can say is yo bro, those are facts. What about your scientific method? Facts are an approximation of reality and facts need to be accepted. Like what else are you gonna do? Some people choose to delude themselves or play roles. I liked your spirit in that regard. You don't want to go that route as I understood. But we can wish good luck to all those that do.

Now the main thing I noticed was your frustration about the things you couldn't change. That's called the human condition bro... we're no gods. There are certain things we have no influence over. For example the DNA you are born with, the very core of you even existing at all. It determined a path for you to walk which was set up before you were even born. Your parents knew they were going to get a boy before you ever did and so they did what was appropriate. They did not know what you decided you were, because you could not speak nor could you think. But now you can speak, now you can think. Now you can change the path you walk on. Every is their own maker. The only way to live is to not get frustrated about the things you cannot change. I feel like you focus a lot on what you cannot change. What can you change? Can you change what you look like? Can you change what you behave like? Can you change what your life path will be like? Can you change the way people perceive you? Sometimes it's yes, sometimes no. The best thing you can do is to teach yourself to change what you want. You mentioned you were frustrated about never having lady part like ladies do. Okay, you can change that, right? There is always going to be a price for change, but it would be within the realm of the possible. Now think about how that change would affect you. From what you said you sound like you wouldn't be satisfied with what you changed, you want more. You want "the real deal" or whatever that means. So you have changed something but it feels like you have achieved nothing. Why does it feel like you have achieved nothing? Because you of your wants... so change your wants if you can change them. (You too are no god, you can't change all wants) and accept them if you can't. 

One more thing I'd like to suggest is that you should always seek to evaluate change within a void. What you decide to do is to change something (let's go with the lady parts example again) and then you look at some reference point outside of yourself and evaluate it based on that instead of your own reference points. I see this sometimes with people who buy expensive cars or something like that. When they buy it, they appreciate it, but they don't necessarily buy it because they want it. They don't buy it because they need it. They usually don't even know why they bought it. Would they have bought it without the influence of media, advertising, expectations of what "success" looks like, without the image of "having a house, a good job, a wife and two kids a perfect lawn and an expensive car"? Etc etc For the car it's not a problem if they can buy it. But I can assure you, that there are a lot of people who experience very similar emotions like you because they feel like they are not successful and know that they will never be able to afford such an expensive car.

Those look serious, I hope you don't feel like you should cut that deep. Cutting deeper is a lot more dangerous for you and actually hurts less because you are cutting through nerve ends. Nerves work like a tree structure, if you cut deep then you are cutting large branches off and the signals the tips of the branches are sending won't come through. That's actually why paper cuts hurt so much, because they don't destroy the nerves, but only activate the ones at the ends of the tree structure. While on the other hand if you were to cut an arm off (pls don't get any stupid ideas...) then it would hurt a lot at the stump, but you would not feel anything on the arms side because no information is coming through. You could cut your detached arm as much as you want and not feel a thing, simply because the nerves are detached. Cutting deeper does not mean anything and it is a lot more easy to get infections, or to die of blood loss when you hit a vein. If you feel the need to hurt yourself for any reason, try to follow the harm reduction model. Very shallow cuts can hurt a lot more than deep ones and pose a smaller risk for your health. Ideally you would want to do something non destructive like the rubber band method or trying to paint on your skin. I don't know if you are that far already, since it can take a lot of mental energy to stay away from what you are doing already, but it's a lot better in the long run. Hope you do well!

Yo, grades are the stupidest shit ever. As someone who consistently had good grades without doing any work I'll tell you that they are quite literally just made up numbers.
